items.title: fix(codex): preserve native threads after interrupted compaction (#13…
items.summary: fix(codex): preserve native threads after interrupted compaction (#138473) Recover the same Codex native thread when compaction commits a host successor but interruption leaves the binding at its recorded predecessor. The host already persists previousSessionId atomically; synchronous native ownership and asynchronous admission now use that fact and the existing conditional binding update. Forward the admitted store and retain the verified host-generation check through ordinary attempts, lifecycle, side questions, native compaction, and manual-resume queue/lease/RPC waits. Carry the recovered generation assertion in private Codex attempt context while preserving the original host-capability object and its core-owned private registrations. Adoption rewrites only the generation fence. Preserve native ownership, catalog refusal, cancellation/reconnect behavior, and unrelated-generation policy. Use the admitted store for manual-resume auth and preserve displaced native ownership across awaited release. Remove the after-compaction adopter and duplicate recovery. Guard startup binding clears after filesystem waits and settle known compaction rejection before restoration, so revoked authority cannot clear a binding and failed restoration cannot leak its completion watcher. Fence unconfirmed remote retirement and post-agent_end coverage/cleanup against a later host generation. Settle known pre-write rejections without waiting for a nonexistent compaction turn. Inline the single-use coverage wrapper so successor messages stay visible on the next saved-thread resume. Failing-before regressions cover interruption, cold saved-ID resume, other generations/owners, and post-adoption host-only rotation. Fixes #137914. Thanks to @vincentkoc for the report and the draft in #138184. Co-authored-by: Vincent Koc Co-authored-by: Vincent Koc
